findings.claim: check.sh's own comment claims it is "written to be wired into CI or a pre-push hook unmodified," but nothing in either repo actually invokes it — it is a purely manual gate.
findings.evidence: musicbox/scripts/check.sh:3-5: "Exits nonzero on any failure so it can be wired into CI or a pre-push hook unmodified." Neither musicbox nor pings has a .github/ directory (confirmed via find). `ls -la .git/hooks/` in both repos shows only the stock *.sample files — none installed as an active hook. Neither repo has a Makefile or .pre-commit-config.yaml. The only references to check.sh outside scripts/ are narrative lines in docs/HISTORY.md and docs/STATUS.md ("bash scripts/check.sh exits 0", "Gate, all green as of 2026-08-31") documenting a one-off manual run, not a wiring mechanism. pings/scripts/check.sh carries the identical unwired pattern (its own header calls itself "the full pings gate" with no CI/hook reference either).
findings.fix: Either add a lightweight .github/workflows/check.yml (or GitLab/other CI equivalent) that runs `bash scripts/check.sh` on push/PR, or install a real pre-push hook (e.g. via a committed `.githooks/` dir plus `git config core.hooksPath`) and document the one-time setup step in README. Until then, drop the "wired into CI" framing from the comment so it doesn't overstate what actually runs.

findings.claim: The systemd service units carry zero process-sandboxing directives (no ProtectSystem=, NoNewPrivileges=, PrivateTmp=, ProtectHome=, RestrictAddressFamilies=, etc.), even though music-import runs flac/ffmpeg/bsdtar over untrusted contributor-uploaded files — the same attack surface the cloud-init comments explicitly call out as needing careful handling.
findings.evidence: systemd/music-import.service, music-backup.service, and musicbox-ping-failure@.service each contain only [Unit]/[Service] boilerplate (Type=oneshot, User=music, EnvironmentFile, ExecStart) — no [Service] hardening keys at all (grep for ProtectSystem/NoNewPrivileges/PrivateTmp across systemd/ returns nothing). cloud-init/user-data.yaml's own comment (lines 206-212) explicitly frames flac/ffmpeg as parsing "untrusted contributor uploads" and a "codec-parsing attack surface." The gap is already named, unfixed, in the estate's own charter: specs/2026-08-30-architecture-refinement-charter.md:26-28 lists "systemd hardening directives not yet applied (ProtectSystem, NoNewPrivileges)" as an open item.
findings.fix: Add a baseline hardening block to all three units: NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict (with ReadWritePaths= for /srv/music and /run/musicbox), ProtectHome=yes, PrivateTmp=yes, ProtectKernelTunables=yes, ProtectControlGroups=yes, RestrictSUIDSGID=yes. Since this is already a named charter item, folding it into the next pass is fine — flagging here so it isn't lost.

findings.claim: None of the three services (navidrome, filebrowser, cloudflared) define a healthcheck:, so `restart: unless-stopped` can only recover from a process exit — a hung-but-alive process (most plausibly cloudflared's tunnel silently dropping while the container itself keeps running) never triggers a restart.
findings.evidence: grep for "healthcheck" across compose.yaml returns no matches. The tunnel is the sole ingress path for both public hostnames (compose.yaml's own header comment: "the only way either is reachable from the internet"), making cloudflared the single highest-value target for a liveness probe, yet it has none.
findings.fix: Add healthcheck: blocks — for navidrome, curl against the loopback-bound /ping or /rest/ping endpoint already exposed at 127.0.0.1:4533; for filebrowser, curl its root over the internal network; for cloudflared, `cloudflared tunnel ready` or a metrics-port check — each with restart-triggering failure thresholds.

findings.claim: No service sets cap_drop, security_opt: no-new-privileges:true, or read_only — filebrowser (the direct entry point for untrusted contributor uploads) and cloudflared (terminates all external traffic) run with Docker's full default capability set on a box whose stated global constraint is enforcing SELinux.
findings.evidence: grep for cap_drop/no-new-privileges/read_only across compose.yaml returns no matches. The volumes already carry the :Z SELinux relabel (per the file's own header comment), which governs file-label access only — it does not restrict process capabilities, and nothing else in the file does either.
findings.fix: Add `security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true]` and an explicit `cap_drop: [ALL]` (re-adding only what each image genuinely needs, e.g. NET_BIND_SERVICE if any service binds <1024) to filebrowser and cloudflared at minimum; consider read_only: true plus a tmpfs mount for any service that doesn't need to write outside its declared volumes.

findings.claim: Neither timer sets RandomizedDelaySec, an idiomatic systemd-timer directive that both softens the fixed-instant OnCalendar= drift into a healthchecks-monitored job and reduces predictability of a job that runs every 15 minutes.
findings.evidence: systemd/music-import.timer and systemd/music-backup.timer each define only OnCalendar=/Persistent=true/Unit= in [Timer] — no RandomizedDelaySec anywhere in systemd/ (grep confirms zero hits).
findings.fix: Low value on a single box with no fleet thundering-herd concern; add RandomizedDelaySec=60 (import) / RandomizedDelaySec=300 (backup) only if it's cheap to bundle with other timer edits, not worth a dedicated pass.

findings.claim: The only firewall rule opens tcp/22 to 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 unconditionally, and nothing in the estate (cloud-init, compose, or a systemd unit) configures fail2ban, sshguard, or sshd's own rate-limiting (MaxAuthTries/PerSourcePenalties) to blunt internet-wide SSH scanning against that fully open port.
findings.evidence: scripts/firewall-rules.json's single rule has source_ips ["0.0.0.0/0", "::/0"] with no narrower CIDR option offered anywhere in provision.sh. Grep across the musicbox tree for fail2ban/sshguard/MaxAuthTries/rate-limit returns zero hits. Key-only auth (ssh_pwauth: false, PasswordAuthentication no) mitigates credential compromise but doesn't reduce the scan/CVE surface the open port presents.
findings.fix: Add dnf-automatic-covered fail2ban (or Alma's built-in sshd rate-limiting via PerSourcePenalties in sshd_config) as a cloud-init write_files/runcmd addition; low urgency given key-only auth already closes the highest-value attack path.

findings.claim: music-beet's lock-file default was never updated in the Task 4 live-deploy fix round that changed music-import's, so the two scripts now lock different files and no longer exclude each other.
findings.evidence: musicbox/scripts/music-import:32 defaults LOCK_FILE to `${MUSICBOX_IMPORT_LOCK_FILE:-/run/musicbox/musicbox-import.lock}` (changed in the 2026-08-31 'Task 4/6: first live deploy' fix round per docs/HISTORY.md item 3, because /run/lock is root:root 0755 on Alma and the `music` user can't create a file there; the unit gained `RuntimeDirectory=musicbox`). musicbox/scripts/music-beet:8 still defaults to the pre-fix path `${MUSICBOX_IMPORT_LOCK_FILE:-/run/lock/musicbox-import.lock}`. music-beet's own header comment claims it 'Blocks on the same lock music-import uses' -- that guarantee is now false: the two scripts flock two different files, so an interactive `music-beet` session and a scheduled `music-import` run can execute concurrently against the same beets database, the exact race the lock exists to prevent. `grep -rn MUSICBOX_IMPORT_LOCK_FILE musicbox/scripts` shows the two literal defaults side by side. There is no music-beet.bats or any test coverage that exercises music-beet's actual lock path (tests/ contains only lib.bats and music-import.bats), which is why the drift was never caught.
findings.fix: Update music-beet's LOCK_FILE default to /run/musicbox/musicbox-import.lock, and better, stop defining the default twice: derive it once (e.g. a shared constant in lib.sh, or have music-beet source the same MUSICBOX_ROOT-relative logic music-import uses) so the two scripts cannot diverge again. Add a bats case that runs music-beet against a held music-import lock and asserts it actually blocks.

findings.claim: music-sync is dead code left over from the superseded workstation-master architecture: the current spec says it 'is replaced by music-pull', but music-pull was never built and music-sync is still live and stowed, contradicting the new single-master (musicbox VPS) design.
findings.evidence: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-30-music-vps-build-design.md:150-158 ('Workstation changes'): '`music-sync` (committed 2026-08-30, laptop-pushes-to-replicas) is replaced by `music-pull`... the workstation beets no longer masters anything.' `find ~/.dotfiles -iname '*music-pull*'` returns nothing -- music-pull was never created. `.dotfiles/bin/.local/bin/music-sync` still exists (mtime Aug 30, unchanged since the old spec) and still does exactly what the new spec says to stop doing: `rclone sync "$LIBRARY" "musicr2:$R2_BUCKET"` writes ~/Music straight into the R2 bucket root (no prefix), using MUSIC_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET -- a *different* credential pair, remote name, and path layout than musicbox/scripts/music-backup's `rclone sync $LIBRARY_DIR $R2_REMOTE:$R2_BUCKET/library` (MUSICBOX_R2_*, prefixed 'library/', with --backup-dir archiving). Two scripts now write to the same bucket under different layouts with the master-ownership question unresolved for music-sync's half.
findings.fix: Either delete/unstow music-sync now that the VPS is the canonical master (nothing in ~/Music needs pushing since 'the workstation beets no longer masters anything'), or, if Geoff still wants a workstation contributor/mirror script, build the documented music-pull (read-only rclone copy of library/ down to ~/Music) and retire music-sync in the same pass rather than leaving both the stale script and the promised replacement absent.

findings.claim: deploy.sh's /etc/msmtprc and /etc/musicbox/contributors.yaml install steps are near-identical ~20-line check/diff/install blocks that differ only in path, mode, and owner -- exactly the kind of block a designed-whole deploy.sh would factor into one function.
findings.evidence: Lines 151-173 (msmtprc) and 175-198 (contributors.yaml) both: check `ssh -o BatchMode=yes ... true` reachability, `diff -q` the local file against a `cat` of the remote path inside `--check`, print 'no changes' / 'would install ...' / "can't reach ... to diff", and otherwise rsync to a /tmp scratch path then `install -m <mode> -o <owner> -g <group> ... && rm -f`. The env-file block just above (lines 129-149) follows the same check/diff/install shape a third time, rendered in-memory instead of via rsync-to-tmp. None of the three share a helper.
findings.fix: Extract a `deploy_file <local_path> <remote_path> <mode> <owner:group>` (or similar) function that runs the check-only diff-and-report branch or the rsync-to-tmp-then-install branch, and call it for msmtprc and contributors.yaml; evaluate folding the env-file block into the same shape.

findings.claim: musicbox's and pings' provision.sh scripts are architecturally the same role (the one script in each repo that talks to its cloud provider) but have inconsistent idempotency/dry-run contracts: musicbox's is check-before-create with a --check dry-run mode and never mutates an existing resource, while pings' has no --check flag at all and unconditionally rotates ADMIN_TOKEN on every invocation, including a 're-run'.
findings.evidence: musicbox/scripts/provision.sh:24-35 parses --check and every create step (ssh-key, firewall, volume, server) is guarded by an `_exists` check that skips creation entirely when the resource is already there (lines 162-213); --check prints a full plan with no side effects (lines 132-160). pings/scripts/provision.sh has no `--check`/`check_only` anywhere in the file, and its own header comment (lines 8-10) admits the asymmetry: 'Safe to re-run... Note that a re-run still rotates ADMIN_TOKEN, invalidating any copy another session or a running Worker instance holds' (confirmed at lines 101-106: `openssl rand -hex 32 >"$token_file"; wrangler secret put ADMIN_TOKEN <"$token_file"` runs unconditionally, no exists-check). An operator who has internalized musicbox's provision.sh convention (idempotent, safe to preview) and reruns pings' provision.sh expecting the same contract will silently invalidate ADMIN_TOKEN.
findings.fix: Either add a --check dry-run to pings' provision.sh matching musicbox's contract, or split the always-mutating ADMIN_TOKEN rotation into its own explicitly-named script (e.g. rotate-admin-token) so 'provision.sh' means the same thing (safe, idempotent, previewable) in both repos of the estate.

findings.claim: uploader_email() and uploader_name() each independently re-parse contributors.yaml through a fresh yq|jq subprocess pipeline per call instead of sharing one lookup, duplicating the same 'load contributors.yaml as JSON' idiom twice in one file.
findings.evidence: Lines 86-92 (uploader_email): `yq -o=json "$CONTRIBUTORS_FILE" | jq -r --arg n "$user" '.contributors[]? | select(.name == $n) | .email' | head -n1`. Lines 102-108 (uploader_name): `yq -o=json "$CONTRIBUTORS_FILE" | jq -e --arg n "$user" 'any(.contributors[]?; .name == $n)' >/dev/null || return 0`. Both are called per uploader inside quarantine_quality_failures's loop (lines 295-296) and move_skips_and_notify's loop (line 164), so a run with N quarantined uploaders shells out to yq+jq up to 2N times to re-read the same static file.
findings.fix: Parse contributors.yaml to JSON once per script invocation (cache in a variable) and have both functions query the cached JSON via jq, or add one `_contributor_field <user> <field>` helper both call.

findings.claim: check.sh's shebang/directive-sniffing loop to classify scripts/* as bash is speculative generality: every file currently under scripts/ already self-declares via shebang or the `# shellcheck shell=bash` directive, so the heuristic (including its 'no shebang, guess by .sh suffix' fallback) buys no coverage a flat file list wouldn't give, and the sibling pings repo's check.sh does the equivalent job with one hardcoded line.
findings.evidence: musicbox/scripts/check.sh:24-43 loops over `scripts/*`, reads the first line, and branches on shebang pattern vs a `# shellcheck shell=bash` directive vs a bare `.sh`-suffix fallback vs 'some other interpreter, not ours'. The manifest's scripts/ directory (check.sh, deploy.sh, lib.sh, music-backup, music-beet, music-import, musicbox-ping-failure, provision.sh) is 8 files, all bash, all already carrying an explicit bash shebang or the lib.sh directive -- the fallback branches are unexercised dead paths for the repo's actual contents. pings/scripts/check.sh:10-11 achieves the same gate with a flat explicit list: `shellcheck scripts/provision.sh scripts/add-check scripts/remove-check scripts/check.sh tests/stubs/curl tests/stubs/wrangler tests/stubs/secret-set-sh`.
findings.fix: Replace the detection loop with an explicit file list matching pings' pattern, or keep the loop only if new non-bash scripts are actually expected under scripts/ soon -- otherwise the heuristic is complexity paid for a problem the repo doesn't have.

findings.claim: The shared curl stub always exits 0 for a plain (non --config) call, so the exact failure mode music-import's own HISTORY.md claims was hardened against — 'a slow or flaky healthchecks.io can never be the reason an otherwise-successful run hangs or gets misreported as failed' — is completely invisible to the suite, and the production code does not actually guarantee it.
findings.evidence: scripts/lib.sh's ping_hc() ends with a bare `curl -fsS --retry 3 --max-time 10 -o /dev/null "$url"` (line 107), no `|| true`. scripts/music-import calls it unguarded three times: `ping_hc import` at line 64 (lock-held path), `ping_hc import fail` at line 394, and the terminal `ping_hc import` at line 406 with nothing after it. Under `set -euo pipefail`, if that curl ultimately fails (healthchecks.io down/unreachable after all 3 retries), ping_hc returns nonzero and the whole script — and, at line 406, an otherwise fully-successful import — exits nonzero, exactly the misreport the retry/max-time hardening (HISTORY.md 'Task 2 follow-up') was supposed to prevent. tests/music-import.bats's stub `curl` (lines 66-84) unconditionally prints '' and exits 0 for every call except the CURL_FAIL_STARTSCAN-gated --config path, so no test in the suite ever exercises a failing plain curl call, and this gap between documented intent and actual guarantee is undetectable by the current suite.
findings.fix: Add a stub-curl failure mode for the plain (no --config) ping_hc shape (e.g. a marker file forcing a nonzero exit), and a bats case asserting that a healthchecks.io failure on the final success ping does not mask/override the fact the import itself succeeded (or, if the intended behavior really is 'fail the whole run', document that explicitly and drop the 'never misreported' language) — then decide, in code, whether the terminal ping_hc calls need `|| true` to match the stated contract.

findings.claim: The admin API's createCheck validates periodMin/graceMin only by `typeof`, not range, so a periodMin of 0 or negative sent directly to POST /admin/checks is silently accepted — unlike scripts/add-check's client-side check, which rejects periodMin < 1 before the request is ever sent — and no test at the Worker layer exercises this boundary.
findings.evidence: src/index.ts lines 56-64 check only `typeof body.periodMin !== "number"` (and same for graceMin); there is no `>= 1` or `>= 0` guard, so `{periodMin: 0}` or `{periodMin: -5}` both pass validation and get persisted as a check's alarm period. test/integration.test.ts's only admin-create-validation case (lines 145-157, 'accepts graceMin: 0') exercises the falsy-zero fix but never a periodMin boundary; scripts.bats's periodMin-rejection tests (tests/scripts.bats lines 61-76) only prove the client-side script rejects it before the request is sent, leaving the server-side contract itself unverified and effectively untested for an out-of-range value.
findings.fix: Add a Worker-level test posting periodMin: 0 (and a negative value) directly to /admin/checks and assert either a 400 or, if 0/negative really is meant to be accepted server-side, document why the client and server disagree on the boundary.

findings.claim: The falsy-zero bug class (fixed twice in this repo's history: admin-validation truthiness, and armingMin defaulting) is patched only at the input-validation boundary, never proven at the arithmetic layer that actually consumes graceMin/armingMin — test/logic.test.ts never exercises transition() with graceMin: 0 or armingMin: 0, so a future `??` → `||` regression in either src/index.ts's `body.armingMin ?? body.periodMin` or the DO's arithmetic would not turn any test red.
findings.evidence: test/logic.test.ts's pushState() helper (lines 6-19) defaults graceMin: 15, armingMin: 60 and no describe block overrides either to 0; overdueAt()/handleAlarm() (src/logic.ts lines 83-86, 149-160) both multiply armingMin/graceMin directly into deadline math. The only graceMin:0/armingMin:0 coverage anywhere in the suite is the acceptance-only check in test/integration.test.ts (POST returns 201) and tests/scripts.bats's 'accepts graceMin of 0' (also acceptance-only) — neither asserts the resulting deadline is actually computed correctly with the zero value.
findings.fix: Add logic.test.ts cases for graceMin: 0 (overdue fires exactly at periodMin, not periodMin+something) and armingMin: 0 (never-armed alert fires immediately), closing the falsy-zero class at the layer where the arithmetic actually lives, not just at the API-acceptance boundary.

findings.claim: Every remove-check test case registers and removes a push check; no test ever removes a pull check, which masks that remove-check's belt-and-suspenders KV cleanup omits `pull:<name>` even though the Worker's own deleteCheck deletes it server-side — the one KV record with no client-side fallback if the admin DELETE itself fails is exactly the one type of check the suite never exercises through remove-check.
findings.evidence: tests/scripts.bats's three remove-check tests (lines 163-191) all use `--period 60 --grace 10`, i.e. push checks. scripts/remove-check's delete_kv_key calls (lines 70-71) cover only `check:$NAME` and `route:$NAME`; src/index.ts's deleteCheck (lines 106-118) additionally deletes `pull:${name}`. A pull check's `pull:<name>` KV record therefore has no belt-and-suspenders coverage if the admin DELETE 404s, and no bats case can catch it because a pull check is never added-then-removed anywhere in the file.
findings.fix: Add a remove-check bats case using a pull check (--pull/--expect-body), asserting pull:<name> is gone after removal, and add a `delete_kv_key "pull:$NAME"` call to scripts/remove-check to close the actual asymmetry the missing test would have caught.

findings.claim: The 'uploader unknown to contributors.yaml' branches are entirely untested: music-import has four distinct code paths that fire when an inbox directory name matches no contributors.yaml entry (two in move_skips_and_notify, two in quarantine_quality_failures), and the fixture's two hardcoded contributors (alice, bob) mean this realistic scenario — a stale FileBrowser account, a typo'd directory — can never be reached by any existing test.
findings.evidence: scripts/music-import lines 169 ('no email on file for uploader'), 298 (same, quality-gate path), and 300 ('no contributor name on file for uploader') have no corresponding bats case; only line 306 (missing reject-email template) is covered ('quality gate: a missing reject-email template...' test). Every stage_good_album/stage_bad_album helper in tests/music-import.bats hardcodes `inbox/alice/...`, and setup()'s contributors.yaml only ever defines alice and bob, so no test ever stages an inbox dir under an unregistered name.
findings.fix: Add a bats case staging an upload under an inbox directory name absent from contributors.yaml, through both the beets-skip path and the quality-gate path, asserting the item still lands in review/quarantine (never silently dropped) and that Geoff's summary still fires even though the uploader-specific email is skipped.

findings.claim: The 'COULD NOT MOVE BY ANY MEANS' fallback branch (both safe_mv_to_review attempts fail) remains self-acknowledged as untested since it was introduced, and stays that way — it is the deepest tier of the same set-e-in-pipeline/mv-collision class two prior fix rounds already patched twice, so leaving its last tier permanently unverified is a live gap in exactly the class this repo has been bitten by repeatedly, not a new one.
findings.evidence: scripts/music-import lines 275-279's else branch (`geoff_summary+="$album_key: COULD NOT MOVE BY ANY MEANS..."`) has no bats case; HISTORY.md's 'Task 2 follow-up, fix round' entry says outright '...a distinct all-caps marker for the (untested, believed-unreachable without a fully read-only filesystem) case where even the fallback fails.' Only the single-failure case (chmod 0555 on review only) is exercised by 'quality gate: an album that can't be moved to review...'.
findings.fix: Force both safe_mv_to_review destinations to be unwritable in one test (chmod 0555 on both review/ and quarantine-failed/'s parent) and assert the all-caps Geoff marker fires and the run still completes to the closing ping.

findings.claim: The 'provision.sh fails when the deployed worker doesn't answer live' test sets PROBE_RETRIES=1 but never proves the override actually took effect — with PROBE_SLEEP=0 the same assertions would pass identically at the script's default PROBE_RETRIES=6, so the test pins the failure message, not the retry-count contract its own env vars advertise.
findings.evidence: tests/scripts.bats lines 243-251: `run env PROBE_RETRIES=1 PROBE_SLEEP=0 "$PROVISION"` then only checks status and the 'expected 404' message; the stub always answers probe-not-live regardless of attempt count (tests/stubs/curl lines 31-34), so nothing distinguishes 1 retry from 6, and a regression that stopped honoring PROBE_RETRIES entirely would not be caught here.
findings.fix: Have the stub log a call count for the probe path and assert it equals PROBE_RETRIES, or drop the PROBE_RETRIES=1 override from this test's framing since it is not actually being tested.

findings.claim: The import lock path is a three-way shared invariant with three independent copies, and music-beet still holds the pre-fix path — so the interactive wrapper and the timer take different locks and no longer exclude each other.
findings.evidence: music-beet:7 `LOCK_FILE="${MUSICBOX_IMPORT_LOCK_FILE:-/run/lock/musicbox-import.lock}"` vs music-import:32 `LOCK_FILE="${MUSICBOX_IMPORT_LOCK_FILE:-/run/musicbox/musicbox-import.lock}"`. The path moved in fix round 3 (docs/HISTORY.md, "Task 4/6: first live deploy", item 3: `/run/lock` is root:root 0755 on Alma, so `RuntimeDirectory=musicbox` was added to systemd/music-import.service and the script default repointed) and music-beet was not updated. deploy.sh:25 installs both scripts, so both ship. Geoff runs music-beet over SSH as root, where creating /run/lock/musicbox-import.lock succeeds — a different file, so flock grants it while music-import holds its own.
findings.fix: Move the lock path to scripts/lib.sh as a single exported default (e.g. `MUSICBOX_LOCK_FILE`), source it in music-import and music-beet, and reference the same name in the unit's RuntimeDirectory comment. A bats test asserting both scripts resolve the identical path pins it.

findings.claim: ping_hc's failure path sends GET to `<url>/fail`, but the pings Worker that now backs these URLs routes `/ping/<slug>/fail` on POST only — so every OnFailure signal from musicbox 404s and is lost.
findings.evidence: lib.sh:104-107 appends `/fail` then `curl -fsS --retry 3 --max-time 10 -o /dev/null "$url"` (no -X POST, no -d). pings/src/index.ts:248 `parts[2] === "fail" && request.method === "POST"`; a GET falls through to line 260 `return new Response("not found", { status: 404 })`. pings/src/check-do.ts:66 is likewise `pathname === "/fail" && request.method === "POST"`. pings/README.md:18 states POST-only is deliberate. pings/docs/STATUS.md:11-14 confirms MUSICBOX_HC_BACKUP_URL/IMPORT_URL/DISK_URL are pings URLs, not healthchecks.io. Consequence: `curl -fsS` exits 22 on the 404, so musicbox-ping-failure@.service itself fails under `set -euo pipefail` and no failure is recorded; the check only alerts later, on silence, after period+grace.
findings.fix: Add `-X POST` (or `--data ''`) to ping_hc's fail branch, and add a cross-repo contract test — either a bats case in musicbox asserting the fail call is a POST, or a pings vitest case asserting GET /ping/<slug>/fail 404s, referenced from musicbox's gate.

findings.claim: music-sync survives on the workstation after the architecture that justified it was superseded, and it is a bucket-root `rclone sync` into the same R2 bucket musicbox backs up to — one secret name away from deleting library/, state/, and _archive/.
findings.evidence: music-sync:41 `rclone sync "$LIBRARY" "musicr2:$R2_BUCKET"` with R2_BUCKET=music-library (line 18) and no --exclude; music-backup:34-36 writes to `$R2_BUCKET/library`, `$R2_BUCKET/state`, `_archive/<tree>/<date>`. The spec explicitly retires it: 2026-08-30-music-vps-build-design.md:152 "`music-sync` (committed 2026-08-30, laptop-pushes-to-replicas) is replaced by `music-pull`: `rclone copy` (never sync)", and plan Task 8 (2026-08-30-music-vps-build.md:208) says "delete `music-sync`, add `music-pull`". The file is still present and stowed (`ls ~/.dotfiles/bin/.local/bin/` shows music-sync, no music-pull), still documents PikaPods SFTP and "laptop is master". Currently inert only because MUSIC_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID/MUSIC_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY are absent from ~/.local/secrets (name-only check) — but MUSIC_R2_RO_ACCESS_KEY_ID/MUSIC_R2_RO_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY exist, so the read-only token minted for music-pull sits unused while the delete-capable script sits armed for the wrong variable names.
findings.fix: Delete music-sync and restow; land music-pull (`rclone copy` of `library/` with MUSIC_R2_RO_*). If the delete is deferred, at minimum make music-sync exit 1 unconditionally with a pointer to music-pull rather than leaving a live sync path.

findings.claim: Each musicbox check's period and grace live only as prose in the pings repo's STATUS, while the timer intervals they are derived from live in musicbox/systemd — two repos, no link, and they have already drifted.
findings.evidence: pings/docs/STATUS.md:13-15 "Registered checks: `musicbox-backup` (period 1560, grace 60), `musicbox-import` (60/15), `musicbox-disk` (60/15)". musicbox/systemd/music-import.timer `OnCalendar=*:0/15` (15 min) against a 60/15 check; musicbox/systemd/music-backup.timer `OnCalendar=*-*-* 11:30:00 UTC` (1440 min) against 1560/60. Nothing in musicbox declares its own check parameters — musicbox/env/musicbox.env.template:30-39 names only URLs — so editing an OnCalendar in musicbox silently invalidates a check nobody in that repo can see. musicbox's plan Task 6 still assigns check creation to musicbox ("Create the four healthchecks.io checks via API"), but the work was done from pings (musicbox/docs/HISTORY.md:44 invokes `~/Projects/pings/scripts/add-check`).
findings.fix: Make musicbox own its check declarations: a `config/checks.yaml` (name, period, grace, kind) committed beside the timers, with a small applier that shells out to pings' add-check. musicbox's gate then diffs the declared periods against the timers' OnCalendar; pings stops holding musicbox facts in prose.

findings.claim: `musicbox-disk` is a live registered push check in pings with no pinger anywhere in musicbox — the check was built in the monitoring repo for a musicbox script that was never written.
findings.evidence: pings/docs/STATUS.md:13-14 registers `musicbox-disk` (60/15). musicbox has no disk-space script or timer: scripts/ contains only check.sh, deploy.sh, lib.sh, music-backup, music-beet, music-import, musicbox-ping-failure, provision.sh; systemd/ contains only music-import.{service,timer}, music-backup.{service,timer}, musicbox-ping-failure@.service; the only ping_hc call sites are `ping_hc import` / `ping_hc backup`. musicbox/docs/STATUS.md:42-44 concedes "MUSICBOX_HC_DISK_URL/MUSICBOX_HC_NAVIDROME_URL are minted but unwired". Per pings/src/check-do.ts:145-147, a push check with no first ping alerts once at createdAt + armingMin (default = period = 60 min) and then stays `alerted` — so this has been reading as a firing check since registration on 2026-08-31, training the reader to ignore it.
findings.fix: Either build the disk-space and Navidrome-heartbeat pingers in musicbox (Task 6's remaining half) or `remove-check musicbox-disk` until they exist. Registering a check before its pinger should not be an accepted state — it manufactures a permanently-red monitor.

findings.claim: The two repos' `scripts/provision.sh` occupy the same slot and name but carry opposite safety contracts: musicbox's is check-before-create with a `--check` dry run, pings' rotates a live secret on every invocation and has no dry-run.
findings.evidence: musicbox/scripts/provision.sh:4-7 "Every resource is check-before-create via `hcloud ... list`, so re-running after a partial failure only creates what is still missing", plus `--check` handling at lines 24-35 and 132-160. pings/scripts/provision.sh:8-10 "Note that a re-run still rotates ADMIN_TOKEN, invalidating any copy another session or a running Worker instance holds"; lines 101-105 unconditionally `openssl rand -hex 32` → `wrangler secret put ADMIN_TOKEN` → secret-set.sh, with no argument parsing and no dry-run path at all. pings/docs/STATUS.md:26-28 records this firing for real: an ADMIN_TOKEN was rotated by re-running provision.sh.
findings.fix: Give pings' provision.sh the same contract: a `--check` mode, and rotation behind an explicit `--rotate-token` flag rather than as a side effect of provisioning. The estate's convention should be one sentence in both headers: `provision.sh` is idempotent and safe to re-run.

findings.claim: `contributors.yaml` is declared the source of truth for four consumers but only one reads it; the Cloudflare Access allow-list, Navidrome accounts, and FileBrowser accounts are hand-applied estate state with no applier and no drift check.
findings.evidence: musicbox/config/contributors.yaml header: "Drives FileBrowser accounts (pass 1), the Access allow-list, Navidrome accounts, and the quality-gate notification map." The only code reading it is music-import's `uploader_email()`/`uploader_name()` (music-import.py lines 86-108) via CONTRIBUTORS_FILE; deploy.sh:175-198 installs it to /etc/musicbox/contributors.yaml and does nothing else with it. Plan Task 5 (line 164) creates the Access policy by hand from the file, Task 8 (line 214) creates accounts by hand. Adding a family member therefore means four manual edits in three systems, with only the email map mechanically enforced.
findings.fix: Make contributors.yaml executable config: a `scripts/apply-contributors` that PUTs the Access policy's email list from the file and reconciles Navidrome/FileBrowser accounts, plus a `--check` diff mode wired into scripts/check.sh. Access-policy application is the half that survives the upload-check pass.

findings.claim: Estate-level Cloudflare state (the tunnel's remote ingress) is parked in musicbox as an inert JSON blob with a curl recipe in a `_comment`, while a working Cloudflare API applier already exists in the pings repo — the applier pattern sits in the repo that needs it less.
findings.evidence: cloudflared-tunnel-config.json's `_comment` field carries a prose curl recipe ("PUT https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/.../cfd_tunnel/<tunnel_id>/configurations, header 'Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN', this object as the JSON body"), and musicbox/docs/STATUS.md:45-48 confirms nothing reads it: "the record of what's PUT to the tunnel's remote config, not something compose.yaml or deploy.sh reads." Meanwhile pings/scripts/provision.sh:47-63 implements `cf_api()` (token off argv via a curl config file) and uses it for DNS, custom-domain, cron and Email Routing reconciliation. Nothing verifies the musicbox file still matches the live tunnel config, and an embedded `_comment` is not a runnable procedure.
findings.fix: Lift `cf_api()` into a shared shell library both repos source (dotfiles scripts/ or a small estate lib vendored into each repo), and add `scripts/apply-tunnel-config.sh --check` to musicbox that GETs the live configuration and diffs it against the committed JSON. Then delete the `_comment` recipe.

findings.claim: The workstation half of Task 8 has fallen out of the ledger because it lands in a different repo: musicbox's STATUS enumerates Task 8's box-side items and silently drops the `music-sync` deletion and `music-pull` creation the plan assigns to .dotfiles.
findings.evidence: musicbox/docs/STATUS.md:51-52 "Task 8 (per-contributor FileBrowser accounts, Navidrome family accounts, seed content, out-of-band credential delivery to Geoff) has not started" — four items. Plan Task 8 (2026-08-30-music-vps-build.md:206-224) lists six, the first being "**Files:** modify `~/.dotfiles/bin/.local/bin/` (delete `music-sync`, add `music-pull`)" plus the spec cross-reference note and the memory update. The dropped items are exactly the ones outside ~/Projects/musicbox, and no dotfiles-side ledger picks them up — which is why finding 3's live music-sync is still stowed.
findings.fix: State the rule in the plan header and in musicbox STATUS: a task with deliverables in another repo carries them in the owning repo's ledger with an explicit repo tag (`[dotfiles]`), and the pass close checks that every plan-task file path appears in some ledger.

findings.claim: The spec chain still assigns monitoring to healthchecks.io while it is implemented as the pings Worker in a separate repo, and musicbox's code and units carry healthchecks.io naming throughout — the substitution happened without the design or the interface names following.
findings.evidence: Spec line 130-131: "Four healthchecks.io checks (free tier): backup success, import-timer success, volume free space, and a Navidrome HTTP heartbeat"; line 148 lists "healthchecks ping URLs" among the secrets. Plan Task 6 line 176-179 likewise says "Create the four healthchecks.io checks via API". Reality: pings/README.md:3 "A small Cloudflare Worker that replaces healthchecks.io for the 907.life estate", and pings/docs/STATUS.md:11-14 holds the registrations. Neither spec nor plan mentions pings at all. The naming persists in code: `MUSICBOX_HC_*` env vars (env/musicbox.env.template:30-39), lib.sh:89/94 "Curls the healthchecks.io URL", music-import:56 "healthchecks.io has no 'this run did nothing' state", both service units' comments, and musicbox-ping-failure:6/15. Finding 2 is the concrete cost: the client was never re-derived against the new server's contract.
findings.fix: Add a superseding note to the spec's Monitoring section pointing at the pings spec, and rename the interface to match reality (`MUSICBOX_PING_*_URL`, `ping_url`/`ping_check` rather than `ping_hc`) in one sweep across lib.sh, the env template, the units, and musicbox-ping-failure. Keep pings' README "Exit path" promise intact — the variable stays a plain URL.

findings.claim: The pings client contract — env-var naming, the no-op-when-unset rule, retry/timeout budget, success-vs-fail semantics — lives in musicbox/scripts/lib.sh, so the second service to adopt pings will reimplement it and drift.
findings.evidence: lib.sh:87-108 `ping_hc` encodes the whole client side: slug→`MUSICBOX_HC_<SLUG>_URL` name derivation (`tr '[:lower:]-' '[:upper:]_'`), "a missing or empty env var is a no-op ... monitoring must never take down the pipeline it monitors", and `--retry 3 --max-time 10`. The pings repo ships the server, the admin scripts (add-check, remove-check) and the exit-path doc, but nothing a consumer can source or copy: pings/README.md:79-85 documents only registration. The naming prefix is hardcoded to MUSICBOX, so the helper cannot even be reused as-is. musicbox's ROADMAP "oss-pair" entry plans to publish pings publicly, which makes the missing client contract an external-facing gap too.
findings.fix: Ship a `client/ping.sh` (or a documented three-line curl snippet plus the naming rule) in the pings repo as the canonical consumer contract, with the fail call's POST spelled out; musicbox's lib.sh sources or vendors it and drops the MUSICBOX prefix assumption.

findings.claim: The two repo gates named scripts/check.sh have diverged in both coverage and failure semantics, so "the gate is green" means something different in each repo.
findings.evidence: musicbox/scripts/check.sh:24-51 discovers bash scripts by shebang/directive/extension and shellchecks whatever is in scripts/; it accumulates `status=1` across shellcheck, bats, docker compose config, and systemd-analyze so every stage runs and all failures are reported (lines 10, 46, 55, 61, 83, 92-97). pings/scripts/check.sh:4 sets `set -euo pipefail` and line 10-11 hardcodes the file list `scripts/provision.sh scripts/add-check scripts/remove-check scripts/check.sh tests/stubs/*` — a newly added script in pings escapes shellcheck silently, and the first failing stage aborts the rest.
findings.fix: Adopt musicbox's discovery loop and status accumulation in pings' check.sh (or extract both to one shared gate helper). At minimum, replace pings' hardcoded list with a glob over scripts/ so a new script cannot escape the linter.

findings.claim: The Cloudflare account ID and the credentials-off-argv curl idiom are estate constants reimplemented independently in both repos, with no shared definition.
findings.evidence: Account ID `120c269ad6d3dfbe6d63a0bb53758ca0` is hardcoded in musicbox/scripts/music-backup:19, .dotfiles/bin/.local/bin/music-sync:17, pings/scripts/provision.sh:17, and inside musicbox/config/cloudflared-tunnel-config.json's `_comment`. The curl-config idiom (write headers/url to a mode-0600 file so the token never reaches argv) is written out four separate times: pings/scripts/provision.sh:47-63, pings/scripts/add-check:174-183, pings/scripts/remove-check (the CONFIG_FILE block), and musicbox/scripts/music-import:342-368. Only the last carries the reasoning comment in full; a fifth writer copying from the shortest version loses the mode-0600 and trap parts.
findings.fix: Put `CF_ACCOUNT_ID` and a `cf_curl`/`curl_with_config` helper in one place both repos read — the dotfiles shell library is the natural home given ~/.local/secrets is already the shared entry point — and reference it rather than recopying.

findings.claim: The superseded PikaPods design carries no forward pointer, so the older spec still reads as current and is the document that keeps music-sync alive.
findings.evidence: 2026-08-30-music-library-design.md opens "The music system masters a FLAC library on the workstation, streams it to family through a Navidrome pod on PikaPods" (line 3) and line 21-23 describes music-sync as the live push tool; nothing in the file marks it superseded. The supersession exists only in the newer file: 2026-08-30-music-vps-build-design.md:6-8 "This supersedes the PikaPods-pod half of `2026-08-30-music-library-design.md`". Both sit in the same specs/ directory with the same date prefix, so a fresh reader has a 50% chance of acting on the retired one — and the plan's Task 8 line 209 explicitly owed this file a "cross-reference note" that was never written.
findings.fix: Add a one-line status banner at the top of the older spec: superseded for the streaming/sync half by the VPS build design, with what still carries over (beets conventions, R2 bucket, clients, one-gatekeeper rule).

findings.claim: pings is framed as an estate-level, eventually open-sourceable monitor but is coupled to musicbox in its tests, its ledger, and its remaining plan tasks — it is a musicbox subsystem wearing an estate-level name.
findings.evidence: pings/test/logic.test.ts:8/156-157 and test/integration.test.ts:294-323 seed fixtures named `musicbox-backup`, `musicbox-navidrome`, `musicbox-disk`; tests/scripts.bats uses `musicbox-x` throughout. pings/docs/STATUS.md:41-43 makes pings' own next task blocked on musicbox Task 6 and assigns "the musicbox script hardening and ledger updates" to pings' plan Task P3 — work in musicbox's tree owned by pings' plan, the mirror of finding 9. musicbox/ROADMAP.md's `oss-pair` entry proposes publishing pings publicly, which makes the coupling a release blocker rather than a cosmetic one.
findings.fix: Rename the fixtures to neutral names (`svc-a`, `nightly-backup`) so the suite stops asserting a single consumer; move P3's musicbox script-hardening item into musicbox's own ledger and leave pings blocked on nothing but its own drill.

findings.claim: Every failure ping is dead: ping_hc sends a GET to /ping/<slug>/fail, but the pings Worker accepts that route only on POST, so the whole OnFailure= chain 404s and no explicit failure ever reaches the monitor.
findings.evidence: lib.sh:105-107 builds `url="${url%/}/fail"` and issues `curl -fsS --retry 3 --max-time 10 -o /dev/null "$url"` with no -X, i.e. a GET. pings/src/index.ts:248 routes fail only when `parts.length === 3 && parts[2] === "fail" && request.method === "POST"`; a GET falls through to `return new Response("not found", { status: 404 })` at index.ts:260, and pings/README.md states the fail route is "POST-only, so a link-scanning mail gateway can never trigger it". `curl -f` therefore exits 22. Consequences: music-backup:41,62,68 and music-import:394 call `ping_hc ... fail` as a bare command under `set -euo pipefail`, so the script aborts on the curl failure before its own `exit 1`; musicbox-ping-failure (the OnFailure= target of both units, systemd/music-import.service:6 and music-backup.service:5) does nothing but `ping_hc "$1" fail`, so that unit fails too and nothing further fires. tests/lib.bats:135-141 asserts the exact broken invocation (`-fsS --retry 3 --max-time 10 -o /dev/null https://hc.example/ping/def456/fail`), so the gate locks the defect in. musicbox env/musicbox.env.template:30-39 still calls these "healthchecks.io ping URLs" while pings/docs/STATUS.md confirms the three MUSICBOX_HC_* values are pings.907.life slugs.
findings.fix: Give ping_hc an explicit method: `curl -fsS -X POST --retry 3 --max-time 10` on the /fail path (leave the success path a GET, which index.ts:245 accepts). Update tests/lib.bats:135-141 to assert the POST form, and correct env/musicbox.env.template's healthchecks.io wording to name the pings Worker.

findings.claim: Every systemd unit runs with zero hardening and with the entire /etc/musicbox/env injected, so the process that parses untrusted contributor uploads holds the Cloudflare Tunnel token and the delete-capable R2 keys it never uses.
findings.evidence: music-import.service, music-backup.service and musicbox-ping-failure@.service each contain only Description/Type/User/EnvironmentFile/ExecStart (plus RuntimeDirectory on import). None carries NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem, ProtectHome, PrivateTmp, PrivateDevices, RestrictAddressFamilies, MemoryDenyWriteExecute, SystemCallFilter, ReadWritePaths, or CapabilityBoundingSet. All three use `EnvironmentFile=/etc/musicbox/env`, which env/musicbox.env.template:13-54 shows carries MUSICBOX_TUNNEL_TOKEN, MUSICBOX_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET, ND_PASSWORDENCRYPTIONKEY, FILEBROWSER_ADMIN_PASSWORD, NAVIDROME_ADMIN_PASSWORD and MUSICBOX_SMTP_PASSWORD. music-import needs only the SMTP password, the Navidrome admin pair, the contributors file and one ping URL, yet it runs bsdtar (lib.sh:61), flac/metaflac (lib.sh:138,151) and beets (music-import:400) over attacker-supplied bytes with the tunnel token and R2 write keys in its environment. musicbox-ping-failure needs exactly one MUSICBOX_HC_*_URL and gets all of it. config/msmtprc:8-17 explicitly reasons about not widening the file's 0600 mode, while the same secrets are handed wholesale to the process anyway.
findings.fix: Split /etc/musicbox/env into per-unit files (env.import, env.backup, env.ping) so each unit gets only what it uses, and add the standard hardening block to all three units: NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict with ReadWritePaths=/srv/music, ProtectHome=yes, PrivateTmp=yes, PrivateDevices=yes, RestrictSUIDSGID=yes, RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_INET AF_INET6 AF_UNIX, LockPersonality=yes. Verify with `systemd-analyze security` and add that to scripts/check.sh.

findings.claim: The spec's "a compromised box can corrupt tomorrow's backup but not erase yesterday's" property is unimplemented: nothing creates the R2 lifecycle rule or the _archive/ object lock, while the box holds a delete-capable key running `rclone sync`.
findings.evidence: The VPS design spec (2026-08-30-music-vps-build-design.md, Backup step 3) requires an R2 object lifecycle rule expiring `_archive/` after 90 days and "an R2 bucket lock on `_archive/` [that] prevents the box's own credentials from shortening or deleting the archive". A repo-wide grep for lifecycle/bucket lock/object lock/versioning across musicbox (excluding docs) returns only music-backup:35-36's `--backup-dir`/`--exclude` flags; docs/ and ROADMAP.md contain no mention at all, so it is neither built nor tracked. music-backup:27-37 runs `rclone sync` (delete-capable) against `music-library/library` and `music-library/state` using MUSICBOX_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET from the box's env file, and lib.sh's own comment chain acknowledges the box is the compromise scenario the archive exists for. Anyone with root or the music user on the box can `rclone delete`/`purge` the whole bucket, including `_archive/`.
findings.fix: Apply the R2 lifecycle rule and object-lock (or bucket-lock) configuration through a committed provisioning step in this repo the way pings/scripts/provision.sh does its Cloudflare wiring, then verify against the live bucket. Until the lock exists, state the residual honestly in docs/STATUS.md rather than leaving the spec's claim standing.

findings.claim: deploy.sh pipes a third-party installer straight into a root shell on the box with no version pin and no checksum, in a repo that already demonstrates the verified pattern for exactly this problem.
findings.evidence: deploy.sh:243-257 runs a heredoc `ssh ... bash -s` as root@HOST containing `command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1 || curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | UV_INSTALL_DIR=/usr/local/bin sh`. No version is pinned and no signature or sha256 is checked, so whatever astral.sh serves at that moment executes as root and lands a binary in /usr/local/bin, which then installs beets for the music user (deploy.sh:255). Contrast cloud-init/user-data.yaml:188-195, which pins yq to v4.53.6 and verifies `sha256sum -c` before `install`, with the comment "pinned to a specific release and checksum-verified against it rather than trusted from a third-party repo". docs/STATUS.md:49-50 exempts uv from the pinning ruling, but that ruling is about version drift and does not address integrity of a root-shell pipe.
findings.fix: Pin the uv version and verify its release checksum before running it, mirroring the yq block in cloud-init; or install uv from a signed repo package. Keep the `command -v` fast path.

findings.claim: The superseded workstation script is still installed and would `rclone sync` ~/Music onto the bucket ROOT, deleting the box's library/, state/ and _archive/ prefixes; its replacement was never written.
findings.evidence: music-sync:41 runs `rclone sync "$LIBRARY" "musicr2:$R2_BUCKET"` with R2_BUCKET="music-library" (line 19) and no prefix, while music-backup:34-35 writes into `music-library/library`, `music-library/state` and `music-library/_archive`. `rclone sync` deletes destination objects absent from the source, so one run from a workstation whose ~/Music no longer masters anything wipes the box's backups and its archive. The VPS design spec's "Workstation changes" section states music-sync "is replaced by music-pull: rclone copy (never sync) ... with the read-only token", yet /var/home/glw907/.local/bin/music-sync is still a live symlink into the dotfiles bin package and /var/home/glw907/.local/bin/music-pull does not exist. Currently defused only by absent credentials: a name-only check of ~/.local/secrets finds MUSIC_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID and MUSIC_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY absent (MUSICBOX_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID present), so today the script skips and exits 1.
findings.fix: Delete music-sync from the dotfiles bin package and restow, and write music-pull as `rclone copy music-library/library -> ~/Music` using a read-only, bucket-scoped token. Do it before any MUSIC_R2_* value is ever minted, since minting one arms the script.

findings.claim: Nothing reconciles contributors.yaml with the live Cloudflare Access policy, so the inbox allow-list drifts silently in both directions; today it grants one of the three listed contributors and there is no revocation path.
findings.evidence: config/contributors.yaml:5-13 lists geoff-login@907.life, oliver@907.life and duncan@907.life, all role: contributor, and its header claims the file "drives FileBrowser accounts (pass 1), the Access allow-list, Navidrome accounts, and the quality-gate notification map". The live probe shows the inbox.907.life Access app has one policy whose include list is the single email geoff-login@907.life, despite a policy name suggesting family membership. No script in the repo reads contributors.yaml for Access purposes: deploy.sh:194-197 only installs it to /etc/musicbox/contributors.yaml for music-import's uploader_email() (music-import:86-92), and no repo file calls the Access API at all. Removing a family member from the yaml therefore revokes nothing, and adding one grants nothing; music-import will happily email an uploader who no longer has access, and an Access include entry survives any repo change.
findings.fix: Make contributors.yaml the single source and drive the Access policy include list from it in a committed script (the same shape as pings/scripts/provision.sh), run from deploy.sh or a dedicated `musicbox-access-sync`, with a --check mode that reports drift. Until then, drop the "drives the Access allow-list" claim from the file header.

findings.claim: safe_extract caps the compressed archive but never the extracted size, and the free-space guard runs only after staging, so one 2 GiB upload can fill the 50 GB volume before any check fires.
findings.evidence: lib.sh:47-51 checks `stat -c%s "$archive"` against max_bytes (default MUSICBOX_MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES=2147483648, music-import:41) and then lib.sh:61 runs `bsdtar -xf "$archive" -C "$destdir"` with no size, member-count, or per-member cap and no `df` re-check between members. music-import:378-389 loops every contributor inbox calling stage_user_uploads (which extracts) and only reaches `free_space_ok "$MUSICBOX_ROOT" "$MIN_FREE_GB"` at line 392, after all extraction is done. A deflate archive of highly compressible content expands orders of magnitude beyond 2 GiB; the spec sizes the Hetzner volume at 50 GB. A full volume then breaks Navidrome's and FileBrowser's state writes (both bind-mounted under /srv/music) and the next backup, and the spec itself names a full disk during import as the truncation hazard it is trying to avoid.
findings.fix: Sum the member sizes reported by `bsdtar -tvf` (or `--totals`) before extraction and reject anything over an uncompressed cap, and re-check free_space_ok between contributors inside the staging loop rather than only after it.

findings.claim: The healthcheck ping URL is a capability token and ping_hc puts it on curl's argv, where any local user can read it from /proc, in the same file that goes to elaborate lengths to keep the Navidrome credential off argv.
findings.evidence: lib.sh:107 is `curl -fsS --retry 3 --max-time 10 -o /dev/null "$url"`, where $url is the full https://pings.907.life/ping/<slug> value. pings/README.md states "A push check's ping URL is as sensitive as the service's own secrets: anyone holding it can keep a dead check green forever." music-import:336-365 already solves this problem for the Navidrome Subsonic credential, writing the URL into a mode-0600 curl --config file with the comment "an argument lands in argv, which every local user can read from /proc or `ps`, but a --config file's contents do not", and pings/scripts/add-check:174-186 and provision.sh:47-63 use the same --config discipline for the admin token. ping_hc is the one place the pattern is not applied, and it runs every 15 minutes.
findings.fix: Reuse music-import's pattern in ping_hc: write `url = "..."` into a mode-0600 mktemp config under the runtime dir and call `curl -fsS -o /dev/null --config <file>`, adding `request = "POST"` for the fail path (see the /fail finding).

findings.claim: quality_gate inspects only `-type f`, so any symlink in an upload skips the only-FLAC gate entirely and is handed to `beet import`, and safe_extract's traversal guard checks member names without ever checking symlink targets.
findings.evidence: lib.sh:156 drives the gate from `find "$dir" -type f -print0`, which excludes symlinks; a symlink named track.flac is therefore never decode-tested by flac -t (lib.sh:138) nor rate/bps-checked (lib.sh:151), and quarantine_quality_failures (music-import:238-324) sees nothing to quarantine, so the containing album goes straight to `beet import -q ... "$STAGING_DIR"` at music-import:400 with beets configured `move: yes` (config/beets-config.yaml:14). Symlinks reach staging either directly (music-import:126 `mv "$entry" "$dest/"` moves whatever the contributor uploaded) or from an archive: lib.sh:53-58 validates only the member path strings via _no_traversal_member (lib.sh:25-35), never a symlink member's target, so containment rests entirely on libarchive's undocumented-here SECURE_SYMLINKS default rather than on this repo's own guard.
findings.fix: Reject symlinks at intake: make stage_user_uploads skip or quarantine `-type l` entries, extend quality_gate's find to `\( -type f -o -type l \)` and fail any symlink, and have safe_extract reject archives whose `bsdtar -tvf` listing contains link members. State the bsdtar security-flag reliance in safe_extract's comment.

findings.claim: The nightly backup pushes navidrome.db, which by design holds reversibly-encrypted family passwords, into the same bucket the workstation's intended read-only mirror token can read, because R2 tokens scope per bucket and not per prefix.
findings.evidence: music-backup:54-58 snapshots $NAVIDROME_DB into staging and line 66 syncs that staging dir to `music-library/state`. compose.yaml:28-31 and the VPS design spec both record that ND_PASSWORDENCRYPTIONKEY exists precisely "because Subsonic token auth forces the server to keep passwords recoverable", so navidrome.db contains decryptable user credentials. The spec's Secrets section provisions "a separate read-only token for the workstation (mirror pull)" bucket-scoped to music-library; R2 API tokens are scoped per bucket, so that token reads state/ as well as library/. Any copy of the mirror token, on any machine, therefore reaches the family's password store; only the separately-held encryption key (which lives in /etc/musicbox/env and is not backed up) stands between it and plaintext.
findings.fix: Split the state backup into its own bucket (say music-library-state) so the workstation mirror token cannot reach it, or encrypt the sqlite snapshots client-side (age, with the key in the workstation store) before the rclone sync. Record whichever is chosen in the spec's Secrets section.

findings.claim: The inbox runs on a single shared FileBrowser admin account whose password sits in the compose environment, so per-contributor isolation currently exists only in config comments and Cloudflare Access is the sole per-person boundary.
findings.evidence: compose.yaml:48-53 passes FILEBROWSER_ADMIN_PASSWORD to the container, and config/filebrowser.yaml:59-63 states "No admin account is minted here. FileBrowser Quantum creates a first-run default on an empty database ... Task 8 immediately replaces it with a real admin account and rotates the password out of band." docs/STATUS.md:51-52 confirms "Task 8 (per-contributor FileBrowser accounts ...) has not started", so the createUserDir/defaultUserScope isolation described at filebrowser.yaml:9-18 is unexercised: whoever gets past Access lands on an admin account with full scope over /srv/music/inbox (compose.yaml:55) and, per userDefaults at filebrowser.yaml:47-56, delete rights. The live Access policy currently includes one email, which is what is actually containing this.
findings.fix: Belongs to the upload-check pass, which replaces this path entirely. Until it lands, treat the admin password as a live shared credential in the registry, and do not widen the Access include list beyond Geoff while one shared account is the only identity.

findings.claim: The whole deploy path is root-over-SSH with no unprivileged deploy account, so every routine config push runs with full box authority and any compromise of the workstation key is total.
findings.evidence: cloud-init/user-data.yaml:10-16 sets `disable_root: false` and installs Geoff's key as root's only authorized key; no other login account is created (the music user is `-s /usr/sbin/nologin`, line 126). deploy.sh:72 sets `SSH_TARGET="root@$HOST"` and every step (rsync into /usr/local/bin and /etc/systemd/system, `install` of /etc/musicbox/env, docker compose up, systemctl enable, the uv root-shell pipe at line 251) runs as root. deploy.sh:32-33 additionally leaves a ControlPersist=60s master socket at $HOME/.ssh/musicbox-deploy-*, so a 60-second window of key-free root access to the box follows every run on the workstation.
findings.fix: Create an unprivileged deploy user with a targeted sudoers entry for the handful of privileged actions, set PermitRootLogin no in the sshd drop-in alongside PasswordAuthentication no, and shorten or drop ControlPersist for the deploy path.

findings.claim: Three deploy steps stage config through fixed, predictable /tmp paths on a box with an unprivileged local user, briefly exposing contributor PII and inviting a pre-created-path race.
findings.evidence: deploy.sh:169 rsyncs config/msmtprc to $SSH_TARGET:/tmp/musicbox-msmtprc, :194 contributors.yaml to /tmp/musicbox-contributors.yaml, and :241 beets-config.yaml to /tmp/musicbox-beets-config.yaml, each then `install`ed and removed. The names are constant across every run, and the files land with rsync's source permissions in world-readable /tmp before the install fixes the mode: contributors.yaml carries every family member's email, which deploy.sh:175-179's own comment says must not be world-readable (it installs it 0640 root:music). The `music` user exists on the box and can watch for or pre-create those paths.
findings.fix: Pipe these files the way /etc/musicbox/env is already handled at deploy.sh:147-148 (`printf ... | ssh ... install -D -m ... /dev/stdin <dest>`), removing the /tmp hop entirely; or stage under a `mktemp -d` created on the remote per run.

findings.claim: The Hetzner firewall admits SSH from the entire internet even though a Cloudflare tunnel already terminates on the box and the only legitimate client is one workstation.
findings.evidence: firewall-rules.json:1-8 is a single inbound tcp/22 rule with source_ips ["0.0.0.0/0", "::/0"], and provision.sh:101-116 treats exactly that pair as the correct state, refusing to proceed if a narrower rule is found ("exists but is missing the tcp/22 rule ... Fix by hand"). Key-only auth (cloud-init:39-43) makes brute force a non-issue, but the box still answers every internet scanner on 22, and any future sshd CVE is reachable pre-auth. The design spec explicitly considered and rejected routing SSH through the tunnel on ergonomics grounds; no middle option (Access-brokered SSH, or a narrowed source list) was weighed.
findings.fix: Either narrow source_ips to the workstation's egress ranges with a documented recovery path via the Hetzner console, or put SSH behind cloudflared's Access-brokered `ssh` ingress and keep tcp/22 closed. Relax provision.sh's firewall_rule_present check so a narrower rule is not reported as broken.

findings.claim: /srv/music/state is world-readable and holds the beets library, the msmtp log and every import log, and /etc/msmtprc is installed 0644, so a future non-root account on the box reads operational data and family email addresses for free.
findings.evidence: cloud-init/user-data.yaml:116 runs `chmod 0755 /srv/music/library /srv/music/review /srv/music/state /srv/music/staging`. That state directory holds library.db (config/beets-config.yaml:11), the Navidrome data volume (compose.yaml:34), msmtp.log (config/msmtprc:22) and music-import's per-run logs (music-import:71). deploy.sh:171-172 installs msmtprc `-m 0644`, which msmtprc:1-2 justifies as "world-readable; see below for why that is safe" on the grounds that it carries no password; the mode is defensible for the credential but the reasoning never covers the log path or recipient addresses it points at. Exposure is limited today because root and music are the only accounts, which is exactly the assumption worth writing down rather than relying on.
findings.fix: chmod 0750 the state directory (root:music or music:music) in cloud-init, install /etc/msmtprc 0640 root:music, and create the msmtp log 0640 under the music group. Note the single-account assumption in the runbook so the next added account does not silently inherit read access.

findings.claim: music-beet's mutual-exclusion guarantee with music-import is currently broken: the two scripts default to two different lock files, so an interactive music-beet session and a scheduled music-import run can touch the beets database at the same time despite the header comment's explicit promise that they can't.
findings.evidence: scripts/music-import (line 32) sets LOCK_FILE default to /run/musicbox/musicbox-import.lock -- changed in the 2026-08-31 'Task 4/6' fix round (docs/HISTORY.md, finding #3) specifically because /run/lock is root:root 0755 on AlmaLinux and the music user can't create a file there. scripts/music-beet (line 8) still defaults LOCK_FILE to the old /run/lock/musicbox-import.lock and was never touched by that fix round (grep for 'music-beet' in HISTORY.md shows no entry after the Task 2 landing). Neither env/musicbox.env.template nor any systemd unit sets MUSICBOX_IMPORT_LOCK_FILE, so both defaults apply unmodified on the box and diverge. No test exercises this: tests/music-import.bats always exports MUSICBOX_IMPORT_LOCK_FILE to a shared fixture path (line 17), which masks the mismatch. music-beet is deployed (deploy.sh's SCRIPT_FILES array includes it) and is the tool the runbook and 'music-import doesn't queue up, it skips' design assumes an operator uses for manual/admin beet work.
findings.fix: Point music-beet's LOCK_FILE default at /run/musicbox/musicbox-import.lock (matching music-import), or better, hoist the single lock-path default into lib.sh as one constant both scripts source, so a future path change can't silently drift between them again. Add a bats case that runs both scripts' actual (non-overridden) defaults against each other.

findings.claim: The estate's entire disaster-recovery story is currently unproven end to end: R2 has never received a successful backup (confirmed empty), and Task 7's restore drill -- the plan's own acceptance gate for 'the box is cattle' -- has never run once. No restore script exists anywhere in the repo.
findings.evidence: docs/HISTORY.md's 2026-08-31 'Task 4/6' entry: acceptance check 3e is 'Blocked -- sqlite3/rclone missing on box... R2 confirmed empty via read-only lsjson'; music-backup.service cannot run at all per the same entry. docs/bringup-runbook.md step 8 lists 'Task 7 restore drill' as still a future next action, not something completed. `grep -rn restore` across the whole musicbox tree finds zero restore script or procedure (scripts/ has music-backup but no music-restore); README.md's headline claim 'provisioned from this repo and restorable from R2 alone' is therefore currently untested in both directions -- nothing has ever been backed up, and nothing has ever been restored.
findings.fix: Treat Task 7 (restore drill against a scratch server) as blocking, not just next-in-line: run it as soon as the pending package remediation lands and a real backup succeeds, before onboarding any family member's irreplaceable purchases (Task 8). Until then, STATUS.md's framing should say plainly that R2 currently holds zero recoverable data, not just that the backup script is blocked.

findings.claim: musicbox-disk is registered as an armed push check with nothing in the estate ever pinging it, and pings' own alerting model means this isn't a quiet no-op: it will fire exactly one 'never-armed' email and then go permanently silent, with no further signal short of someone manually reading the weekly digest -- a materially worse state than STATUS.md's 'minted but unwired' framing suggests.
findings.evidence: grep across musicbox for 'ping_hc' shows only music-import and music-backup ever call it (with slugs 'import'/'backup'); nothing calls 'ping_hc disk'. pings/docs/HISTORY.md's P2b entry confirms musicbox-disk was registered live 2026-08-31 with period 60/grace 15 (armingMin defaults to periodMin per src/index.ts line 65, so 60 min). src/logic.ts's handleAlarm (lines 149-155): once a check with lastPing===undefined has alerted once, every later alarm event returns {state, emails: []} unchanged -- there is no code path back to alerted=false except a real ping event (handlePing/handleProbeResult), which this check will never receive until Task 6's disk-space script exists. musicbox/docs/STATUS.md's Open items (lines 42-44) describes this only as 'minted but unwired,' not as an alert that has already fired once and then muted itself.
findings.fix: Either don't register a push check via add-check until its pinging script exists, or (better) change P2c's live drill to explicitly cover and document the never-armed-then-silent behavior so it's a known property, not a surprise. Short term: check whether musicbox-disk's one-time alert already landed and consider deleting/re-registering it once the disk-check script ships, so its arming window restarts cleanly.

findings.claim: STATUS.md's single 'Reprovision pending' Open item conflates two remediations of very different cost and blocking status -- the genuinely dnf-blocked package installs (ffmpeg/flac/sqlite3/rclone/msmtp) and the already-fixed Navidrome scan-trigger script, which needs only an unblocked `deploy.sh` re-run -- making the ongoing 'cron-only, up-to-24h-stale library' state look more blocked than it is.
findings.evidence: docs/HISTORY.md's 2026-08-31 'Spec gaps closed' entry says the Subsonic startScan rewrite is committed but 'Neither fix has reached the already-provisioned live box yet (cloud-init is first-boot-only); see STATUS's reprovision pending open item.' But scripts/deploy.sh's SCRIPT_FILES array (line 25) already includes music-import and lib.sh and rsyncs them to /usr/local/bin on every run -- no dnf install, no reprovision, and none of the Claude Code auto-mode classifier refusals documented for on-box `dnf install` (HISTORY.md lines 86-89) apply to a plain `bash scripts/deploy.sh`. Meanwhile compose.yaml (lines 21-27) confirms ND_SCANNER_SCHEDULE is the only other path music actually becomes visible, once daily at 3am UTC, so every album imported today sits invisible in Navidrome for up to ~24h.
findings.fix: Split the Open items entry in two: one for the cheap, unblocked deploy.sh re-run that lands the scan-trigger fix today, and one for the genuinely dnf-blocked package remediation that needs Geoff present. Running the former immediately shrinks the cron-only staleness window from indefinite to whenever the next deploy.sh runs.

findings.claim: music-backup has no flock (or any) overlap protection, unlike music-import and music-beet, which both serialize against the same lock file; a manual `systemctl start music-backup` run overlapping the daily timer (exactly what the bringup runbook itself instructs at step 4) can race on `$BACKUP_STAGING` (line 45's `rm -rf` deletes the other run's in-flight sqlite .backup output) or on the concurrent rclone syncs to the same R2 destination paths.
findings.evidence: Full read of scripts/music-backup: no `flock`, `exec 200>`, or any lock-file reference anywhere in the file, contrasted with music-import's explicit flock section (lines 61-66) and music-beet's matching flock wait (lines 10-14). The script's own header comment explains why sqlite3 .backup exists (avoiding a torn snapshot of a live DB) but that protection only covers the DB-vs-live-write race, not a second music-backup instance racing the first's staging directory and rclone sync.
findings.fix: Add the same flock pattern used in music-import (a dedicated lock file, non-blocking with a clean skip-and-ping-success exit) to music-backup, so an overlapping manual run during a fix session or drill can't race the scheduled one.

findings.claim: sweep_review() only prunes REVIEW_DIR on a 60-day retention; QUARANTINE_FAILED_DIR (the emergency fallback used when a quality-gate quarantine can't even be filed to review) has no retention sweep at all, so anything that ever lands there accumulates on disk forever with only the one-time creation email as a signal.
findings.evidence: scripts/music-import lines 373-376 (sweep_review) walks only $REVIEW_DIR. QUARANTINE_FAILED_DIR is defined at line 27 with the comment 'Not created up front... a healthy box never has one,' and is only ever written to inside quarantine_quality_failures's fallback branch (lines 267-279), which is deliberately the rare, unverified-in-practice path (the whole quality-gate pipeline has only ever run against an empty inbox so far per the 2026-08-31 acceptance sweep). No later code path reads or cleans this directory.
findings.fix: Extend sweep_review (or add a parallel sweep) to also age out QUARANTINE_FAILED_DIR entries, or at minimum have it surface in the weekly/periodic operational summary so accumulation there isn't purely dependent on someone remembering the one-time email months later.

findings.claim: createCheck() calls PUT /init on the CheckDO stub, then writes the KV records that are the only way to address/find/delete that DO, as two sequential un-batched writes with no rollback; if either KV write fails after DO init succeeds, the DO is left permanently armed and completely unreachable (no name, no route key), so it will alert ALERT_EMAIL hourly forever with no way to delete it via remove-check.
findings.evidence: index.ts:88-103: `const initResponse = await checkStub(env, address).fetch("http://check-do/init", ...); if (!initResponse.ok) return new Response(...500); await env.PINGS_KV.put(`check:${body.name}`, ...); if (push) await env.PINGS_KV.put(`route:${body.name}`, address); ...`. There is no try/catch around the KV puts and no compensating DELETE to the stub on failure. deleteCheck() (index.ts:106-118) can only find a push check's DO via `route:<name>` in KV, so a DO created this way is orphaned. check-do.ts's alarm() (line 80-86) will keep firing 'never-armed' alerts (logic.ts handleAlarm) since lastPing is undefined forever.
findings.fix: Write route:<name>/pull:<name> (the only key that lets deleteCheck find the DO) before or atomically with check:<name>, and wrap the KV writes in try/catch that issues a compensating DELETE to the stub on failure so a partial create never leaves an unreachable armed DO. Alternatively store the slug inside the check:<name> value itself so a single KV write is sufficient and deleteCheck never depends on a second key.

findings.claim: applyTransition() awaits network I/O (the KV-backed daily-cap check and the send_email fetch, via trySend) before persisting the new state with ctx.storage.put — outside the scope of Durable Objects' automatic input/output gates, which only protect ctx.storage operations, not arbitrary fetch()/KV calls, so a second event delivered to the same DO instance during that window can read stale pre-transition state and its later write can clobber the first event's persisted state.
findings.evidence: check-do.ts: fetch() reads state once (line 49) before dispatch; applyTransition (113-124) computes the transition, then `for (const email of result.emails) { const sent = await this.trySend(state, email); ... }` before `await this.ctx.storage.put(STATE_KEY, persisted)` (line 122). trySend (127-139) awaits env.PINGS_KV.get/put and env.EMAIL.send — none of which hold a Durable Object input gate (per Cloudflare's docs, gates wrap ctx.storage.* calls: https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/storage-api/#input-gates-in-durable-objects). An alarm firing at the same instant as an in-flight /ping or /fail POST (or an HTTP client retry sending a duplicate /ping) can interleave and lose a pingCount/failCount increment or bypass the alert cooldown gate since both read the same stale lastAlertAt.
findings.fix: Persist the state transition (ctx.storage.put) before attempting the email send, and treat the send as a best-effort follow-up (retry via the existing past-due alarm fallback) rather than gating persistence on it — this removes the un-gated network await from the read-modify-write window. If the current rollback-on-failure semantics for alerted/lastAlertAt must be kept, consider explicitly serializing with an in-memory in-flight flag checked at the top of fetch()/alarm().

findings.claim: deleteCheck() silently no-ops the Durable Object teardown when the route:<name> KV lookup returns nothing (for a push check), reporting success (200) while leaving the DO's alarm armed indefinitely.
findings.evidence: index.ts:106-118: `const address = meta.kind === "push" ? await env.PINGS_KV.get(`route:${name}`) : name; if (address) await checkStub(env, address).fetch(...DELETE...);` — the DELETE call is entirely skipped, with no error/log, when address is falsy, yet the function proceeds to delete the KV check/route/pull records and return 200 regardless.
findings.fix: Log/return a non-200 (or at least a warning field in the response) when a push check's route key is missing so an operator running remove-check learns the DO teardown did not happen, instead of a clean-looking 200.

findings.claim: probePullChecks() and maybeSendDigest() iterate their KV key lists and DO calls sequentially with `for (const key of list.keys) { await ... }`, so the cron tick's wall time scales linearly with the number of pull/registered checks (up to PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS=10s per pull check); this does not scale and a single slow pull target delays every other check's probe in the same tick.
findings.evidence: index.ts:153-180 (probePullChecks) and 197-212 (maybeSendDigest) both use a plain `for...of` loop with `await` per iteration rather than Promise.all/allSettled.
findings.fix: Parallelize per-check work with Promise.allSettled (bounded by KV/DO subrequest limits), or accept the current sequential design explicitly given the small check count (3-4 musicbox checks today) and note the scaling ceiling in HISTORY/STATUS.

findings.claim: reserveDailyAlertSlot() is a non-atomic KV read-then-write (get count, then put count+1); the code comment characterizes the risk as an 'undercount', but the actual race lets concurrent DOs both read the same sub-cap count and both proceed to send, meaning the effective cap can be exceeded, not just undercounted in the stored value.
findings.evidence: check-do.ts:26-30 comment: 'A concurrent-write undercount is accepted — this is a reputation/quota backstop, not a security control.' Lines 33-41: `const raw = await kv.get(key); const count = ...; if (count >= DAILY_ALERT_CAP) return false; await kv.put(key, String(count + 1), ...); return true;` — two concurrent calls reading count=49 both return true and both send, so more than DAILY_ALERT_CAP emails can be sent even though the stored counter itself ends up undercounting the true send total.
findings.fix: If the cap must be a hard ceiling, use a KV/DO-backed atomic counter (e.g. route the cap through one dedicated DO, or accept and document that the cap is a soft best-effort limit that can be exceeded under concurrency, not just undercounted in its own bookkeeping — current comment undersells the actual failure mode.

findings.claim: scheduleNextAlarm's past-due fallback (dueAt > now ? dueAt : now + RETRY_DELAY_MS) means an --arming 0 push check does not actually arm 'immediately': by the time the comparison runs a few milliseconds have elapsed past createdAt, so dueAt <= now and the check instead waits a full RETRY_DELAY_MS (5 minutes) before its first never-armed alarm evaluation.
findings.evidence: check-do.ts:142-155, specifically line 147 `dueAt = state.createdAt + state.armingMin * MIN_MS;` combined with line 154's `dueAt > now ? dueAt : now + RETRY_DELAY_MS` fallback intended for failed-send retries, which also silently swallows the armingMin:0 immediate-arm case.
findings.fix: Distinguish the 'send failed, retry' case from the 'legitimately due in the past at schedule time' case (e.g. pass an explicit isRetry flag into scheduleNextAlarm) rather than overloading the same now-vs-dueAt comparison for both.
