findings.claim: probe_http_status() calls curl with no --max-time/--connect-timeout, so a hung TLS handshake against the not-yet-live custom domain during the post-deploy probe loop can stall provision.sh well beyond the intended PROBE_RETRIES * PROBE_SLEEP budget (default 6*5=30s).
findings.evidence: provision.sh:131-135: `probe_http_status() { local url="$1"; shift; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$@" "$url"; }` — no timeout flags passed by either call site (lines 140-141).
findings.fix: Add `--max-time 10` (or similar) to the curl invocation so each probe attempt is bounded independently of the retry loop's sleep budget.

findings.claim: check_exists() classifies a missing key purely by grepping wrangler's stderr for a bare '404' (with digit guards); this couples correctness to wrangler's current unstructured error text rather than a structured signal, and a future wrangler version or an unrelated 404 substring in an error message (e.g. a request id) could silently misclassify a real outage as 'absent' or vice versa.
findings.evidence: add-check:123-140, specifically `if grep -qE '(^|[^0-9])404([^0-9]|$)' "$KV_ERR_FILE"; then return 1; fi` — matched against whatever text `wrangler kv key get --remote` happens to print to stderr on a 404, which is not a documented stable contract.
findings.fix: Prefer a structured signal if wrangler exposes one (e.g. `--output json` if/when the KV command supports it) over parsing free-text stderr; failing that, add a comment pinning the wrangler version this was verified against so a version bump is a deliberate re-check, similar to the compatibility_date discipline already used for wrangler.jsonc.

findings.claim: notify() (msmtp) is called as a bare, unguarded statement at every call site inside music-import; a single mail-delivery failure for one contributor aborts the entire import run under set -e, skipping beet import, Geoff's own summary email, the Navidrome scan trigger, sweep_review, and the final healthcheck ping.
findings.evidence: lib.sh:78-85 notify() has no internal error handling and returns msmtp's own exit status. Every call site in music-import is a bare statement, not wrapped in `if`/`||`: lines 166-167 and 172-173 inside move_skips_and_notify, and lines 308-309 and 320-323 inside quarantine_quality_failures. music-import runs under `set -euo pipefail` (line 2), so if msmtp fails for any one recipient (bad/expired address in contributors.yaml, relay outage, malformed From in /etc/msmtprc) the script terminates at that exact statement. Because quarantine_quality_failures already moved the failing album out of staging via safe_mv_to_review before calling notify (lines 267-281), a failure here leaves some albums quarantined and the rest of the pipeline -- including `beet import` at line 400 and the final `ping_hc import` at line 406 -- never run that day.
findings.fix: Wrap every notify() call in `notify ... || echo "...notify failed for $user..." >&2` (mirroring the pattern already used for ping_hc/curl failures), or give notify() itself a best-effort contract (log-and-return-0) so one bad address can never take the run down.

findings.claim: safe_extract has no per-archive isolation: every archive a contributor uploads in one batch is extracted into the same shared per-user staging directory, so two archives (or a loose file and prior staging residue) with a same-named entry at the same relative path silently overwrite each other via bsdtar's default overwrite behavior, or make the subsequent plain `mv` fail outright and abort the run.
findings.evidence: lib.sh:43-62 safe_extract runs `bsdtar -xf "$archive" -C "$destdir"` where destdir is whatever caller passes; music-import's stage_user_uploads (lines 113-130) computes dest once per user (`STAGING_DIR/$user`, set at the call site line 388) and reuses it for every entry in the loop, so a second archive (e.g. a flat Bandcamp zip with `01.flac`/`cover.jpg` at its root, uploaded alongside another flat album in the same batch) extracts on top of the first with no collision check, unlike unique_dest_path/safe_mv_to_review elsewhere in this same file (lines 160-208) which explicitly exist to prevent exactly this overwrite. The non-archive branch (line 126, `mv "$entry" "$dest/"`) has the same gap: colliding with an existing same-named directory makes `mv` fail, which as a bare statement under set -e aborts the whole script.
findings.fix: Extract each archive into its own subdirectory of dest (e.g. named from the archive's basename) before beets sees it, and route the non-archive mv through safe_mv_to_review/unique_dest_path instead of a plain `mv`.

findings.claim: trigger_navidrome_scan's documented "best-effort, never fails the import" contract is only actually implemented for the final curl call; every earlier step is an unguarded bare statement that will abort the whole script under set -e if it fails, contradicting the function's own header comment.
findings.evidence: lib.sh:326-329 states the function is "Best-effort: a failed scan trigger does not fail the import", but only the final `curl -fsS -o /dev/null --config "$config_file" || echo ...; return 0` (lines 367-368) is guarded. The preceding jq call (line 352), the od call for the salt (line 356), `mktemp "$RUNTIME_DIR/navidrome-scan.XXXXXX"` (line 360), and `chmod 0600 "$config_file"` (line 364) are all bare statements. music-import calls the function bare at line 404 (no `|| true`). If /run/musicbox runs low on space or inodes so mktemp fails, or jq is missing/broken, the script aborts there -- after `beet import` already succeeded -- skipping sweep_review (line 405) and the final success `ping_hc import` (line 406), misreporting a fully successful import as a hung/failed run.
findings.fix: Guard the whole function body (e.g. run it in a subshell called as `trigger_navidrome_scan || echo "...scan trigger failed..." >&2` at the call site, or wrap each fallible step) so any failure inside it, not just curl's, is swallowed per the documented contract.

findings.claim: music-backup has no existence/non-empty guard on LIBRARY_DIR before rclone-syncing it to R2, unlike the two database files which are explicitly existence-checked; an unmounted or empty library mount causes the nightly backup to silently archive-away (not literally delete, but remove from the live prefix) the entire off-site library copy while still reporting success.
findings.evidence: Compare music-backup:48-58, which guard BEETS_DB and NAVIDROME_DB with `if [ -f "$BEETS_DB" ]; then ... else echo ...skipping... fi`, against line 60, `if ! rclone_backup_sync "$LIBRARY_DIR" "library"; then`, which has no preceding existence or non-emptiness check on LIBRARY_DIR at all. rclone_backup_sync (lines 27-37) runs `rclone sync "$src" "$R2_REMOTE:$R2_BUCKET/$tree" --backup-dir ...` -- syncing FROM an empty (but present) directory is not an rclone error, it just makes the destination match: every object currently under the R2 "library" prefix gets moved into `_archive/library/$DATE_STR`. If /srv/music/library is an empty mount point because the Hetzner data volume failed to (re)attach on boot, this run exits 0 and calls `ping_hc backup` (line 72) as a success, even though the live off-site copy of the whole library was just emptied.
findings.fix: Add a `[ -d "$LIBRARY_DIR" ] && [ -n "$(find "$LIBRARY_DIR" -mindepth 1 -print -quit)" ]` guard before the library rclone sync, matching the pattern already used for the two DB files, and ping_hc backup fail + exit 1 when it's empty.

findings.claim: ping_hc is called bare at both the lock-contention success path and the final success path; a transient healthchecks.io failure (not a missing URL, which is the only case ping_hc's own doc comment protects against) makes set -e abort the script at that exact point, defeating the explicit design decision quoted in the surrounding comment.
findings.evidence: music-import:51-60's comment states the spec decision is to "treat it as success rather than let a merely-overlapping run page Geoff at 3am", but line 64 (`ping_hc import`) is a bare statement before `exit 0` at line 65; if the MUSICBOX_HC_IMPORT_URL curl call itself fails (network blip, healthchecks.io outage, DNS failure -- distinct from the empty-var no-op case lib.sh:100-103 handles), ping_hc returns curl's nonzero status and set -e terminates the script before reaching `exit 0`, so the lock-contention run reports failure instead of the intended success. The same bare pattern repeats at the final line 406 (`ping_hc import`, after a fully successful pipeline) and in music-backup's final line 72 (`ping_hc backup`).
findings.fix: Guard every terminal ping_hc call with `|| true` (or `|| echo "...hc ping failed..." >&2`) so a monitoring-endpoint hiccup can never change the script's own exit status.

findings.claim: quality_gate dispatches purely on filename extension; a file with no extension or the wrong extension for its actual format is never inspected at all and proceeds straight to beet import, bypassing the FLAC-only/quality invariant the function exists to enforce.
findings.evidence: lib.sh:123-136: the case statement matches only `flac` (pass) and a fixed list of known-bad extensions (fail), with `*) continue ;;` for everything else -- a file whose extension is missing or mismatched from its true codec (e.g. a browser upload that drops the suffix, or a mislabeled MP3) falls into the `*)` branch and is silently skipped, never decode-tested and never sample-rate-checked, then reaches `beet import -q` (music-import:400) unfiltered. The function's own header comment (lines 112-113) states the whole point is "only high-quality FLAC enters the library."
findings.fix: Sniff file type by content (e.g. `file --mime-type` or attempt the flac decode test regardless of extension) rather than trusting the filename suffix, at least as a fallback for files with no recognized extension.
findings.severity_note: may overlap with the planned upload-check/validated-intake pass

findings.claim: trigger_navidrome_scan's temp credential file is cleaned up only via a function-scoped RETURN trap; a SIGTERM/SIGKILL delivered to music-import while this function is executing (e.g. systemd stopping the unit, an operator killing a hung run) never fires that trap, leaving the token-bearing file behind in /run/musicbox until reboot.
findings.evidence: lib.sh:360-365: `config_file="$(mktemp "$RUNTIME_DIR/navidrome-scan.XXXXXX")"` then `trap 'rm -f "$config_file"' RETURN`. A RETURN trap fires only on normal function return, not on a signal that kills the process; there is no corresponding EXIT/TERM trap anywhere in music-import.
findings.fix: Also register the cleanup on `trap ... EXIT` at the top of the script (or at minimum inside this function) so a killed run doesn't strand the credential-derived token file.

findings.claim: free_space_ok is checked only after every pending contributor archive has already been extracted into staging, so the extraction step itself is unbounded by the disk-space guard meant to catch exactly this condition.
findings.evidence: music-import:378-389 runs stage_user_uploads (which calls safe_extract, decompressing every archive in every contributor's inbox) inside the `for user_dir in "$INBOX_DIR"/*/` loop; only afterward, at line 392, does `if ! free_space_ok "$MUSICBOX_ROOT" "$MIN_FREE_GB"; then` run. safe_extract (lib.sh:37-62) caps only the archive's *compressed* size (MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES, default 2GiB) with no cap on decompressed size, so a run can already fill the disk during staging before the guard that exists to prevent low-space conditions ever executes.
findings.fix: Check free_space_ok before stage_user_uploads too (or re-check after each user's extraction), and/or cap extracted size in safe_extract, not just archive size on disk.
